answer: The quill report exposes the merge explicitly at each terrace. The replay builds a funding-and-timing graph over every join and collapses clusters that share a funder, an address prefix, or suspiciously correlated submission times into a single entity. Because of that, an adversary who spins up 149 aliases from one source ends up with the same influence as one agent, paying 147 times the capital for one share. That is 3 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
